name_sw: Samaki wa Kukaanga kwa Mafuta ya Nazi
description: Whole tilapia fried in fragrant coconut oil until crisp, a coastal Kenyan way to enjoy fresh lake fish.

steps.instruction: Clean and score the tilapia. Rub with salt and lemon juice.
Heat coconut oil in a deep pan until hot but not smoking.
Fry the fish for 5–7 minutes per side until golden and crispy. Drain and serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and greens.

description: Fluffy rice cooked with coconut oil and onions, a simple coastal Kenyan side with a subtle tropical aroma.

steps.instruction: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Heat coconut oil and sauté the chopped onion until soft.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute to coat with the oil.
Pour in water and salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 18–20 minutes until the rice is tender.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with fish curry or bean stew.

name_sw: Mboga za Majani kwa Mafuta ya Nazi
description: Kale and spinach wilted in coconut oil with onions and tomatoes, a quick Kenyan side with a coastal twist.

steps.instruction: Wash and chop the kale and spinach. Heat coconut oil and sauté the onion until soft.
Add the chopped tomato (if using) and cook until softened.
Add the greens and salt. Stir-fry for 5–7 minutes until wilted but still bright. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali or rice.

description: Soft layered Kenyan chapati made with coconut oil, giving the flatbread a delicate tropical fragrance.

steps.instruction: Mix flour and salt. Add water gradually and knead into a soft dough.
Divide into 6–8 balls, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll each ball thin, brush with coconut oil, fold into a spiral and roll out again.
Cook on a hot pan for 2–3 minutes per side, brushing with coconut oil, until golden.

serving_suggestion: Serve with bean stew or tea.

description: Beans simmered in a tomato-onion gravy made with coconut oil, adding a gentle sweetness to a Kenyan staple.

steps.instruction: Heat coconut oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic if using.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until they break down into a sauce.
Add cooked beans and salt. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until the stew thickens. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali or chapati.

description: Fragrant rice cooked with ghee and onions, a rich Kenyan side often served at celebrations.

steps.instruction: Rinse the rice. Heat ghee and sauté the chopped onion until golden.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute until coated with ghee.
Add water and salt. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer for 18–20 minutes until tender. Fluff and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with chicken curry or lentil stew.

description: A rich, sticky Kenyan coastal sweet made with ghee, flour, sugar and cardamom.

steps.instruction: Melt ghee in a pan and roast the flour until golden and fragrant, about 8–10 minutes.
In another pot, boil sugar, water and cardamom to make a syrup.
Pour the hot syrup into the roasted flour, stirring vigorously to prevent lumps.
Cook on low heat, stirring, until thick. Serve warm or at room temperature.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a dessert after a coastal meal.

description: Soft Kenyan chapati brushed with ghee, giving the flatbread a rich, buttery flavour.

steps.instruction: Mix flour and salt. Add water and knead into a soft dough. Rest for 30 minutes.
Divide into balls, roll thin, brush with ghee, fold into a spiral and roll again.
Cook on a hot pan for 2–3 minutes per side, brushing with ghee, until golden.

serving_suggestion: Serve with beef stew or tea.

description: Yellow lentils simmered with onions, tomatoes and garlic, finished with a spoonful of ghee.

steps.instruction: Rinse lentils. Heat ghee and sauté onions and garlic until soft.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until softened.
Add lentils, water and salt. Simmer for 20–25 minutes until lentils are soft. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or chapati.

description: Ripe bananas pan-fried in ghee until caramelised, a simple Kenyan dessert or snack.

steps.instruction: Peel and slice the bananas lengthwise or into thick rounds.
Heat ghee in a pan. Fry the bananas for 2–3 minutes per side until golden and caramelised.
Sprinkle with sugar if using and serve warm.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a dessert or snack.

name_sw: Mboga za Majani kwa Mafuta ya Karanga
description: Spinach stir-fried in groundnut oil with onions and tomatoes, a simple Kenyan side with a nutty aroma.

steps.instruction: Heat groundnut oil and sauté the onion until golden.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and saucy.
Add spinach and salt. Stir until wilted, about 5 minutes. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali or rice.

name_sw: Samaki wa Kukaanga kwa Mafuta ya Karanga
description: Tilapia fillets fried in groundnut oil until golden, a simple Kenyan fish dish with a rich, nutty taste.

steps.instruction: Season the tilapia fillets with salt and lemon juice.
Heat groundnut oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the fillets for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Drain and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali and greens.

description: Kenyan chapati made with groundnut oil, giving the flatbread a subtle nutty flavour.

steps.instruction: Mix flour and salt. Add water and knead into a soft dough. Rest for 30 minutes.
Divide into balls, roll thin, brush with groundnut oil, fold into a spiral and roll again.
Cook on a hot pan for 2–3 minutes per side, brushing with oil, until golden.

serving_suggestion: Serve with bean stew or tea.

description: Beans simmered in a tomato-onion gravy made with groundnut oil, a hearty Kenyan staple.

steps.instruction: Heat groundnut oil and sauté onions until golden. Add garlic if using.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add cooked beans and salt. Simmer for 10–15 minutes until thick. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with ugali or chapati.

description: Rice cooked with groundnut oil and onions, a simple Kenyan side with a nutty aroma.

steps.instruction: Rinse rice. Heat groundnut oil and sauté onion until soft.
Add rice and stir for 1 minute. Pour in water and salt.
Bring to a boil, cover and simmer for 18–20 minutes until tender. Fluff and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with fish or bean stew.

description: Creamy avocado tossed with tomatoes, red onion and lemon, a fresh Kenyan side salad.

steps.instruction: Dice the avocado and tomatoes. Finely chop the red onion.
Combine in a bowl and squeeze lemon juice over.
Sprinkle with salt, toss gently and serve immediately.

serving_suggestion: Serve alongside rice, ugali or grilled meat.

description: A sweet and creamy Kenyan salsa of avocado, mango, red onion and lime.

steps.instruction: Dice the avocado and mango. Finely chop the red onion and coriander.
Combine in a bowl and squeeze lime juice over.
Add salt, toss gently and serve fresh.

serving_suggestion: Serve with grilled fish or as a side.

description: A creamy Kenyan smoothie made with avocado, milk and banana, perfect for breakfast.

steps.instruction: Scoop the avocado flesh into a blender.
Add milk, banana and sugar if using.
Blend until smooth and serve chilled.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a breakfast drink.

description: A protein-rich Kenyan salad of avocado, boiled eggs, tomato and onion.

steps.instruction: Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool, peel and chop.
Dice the avocado and tomatoes. Finely chop the onion.
Combine everything, squeeze lemon juice over, season with salt and toss gently.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a light main or side.

description: Kenya's classic tomato-onion kachumbari with creamy avocado folded in.

steps.instruction: Dice avocado and tomatoes. Finely chop red onion and coriander.
Combine in a bowl and squeeze lime juice over.
Add salt, toss gently and serve fresh.

serving_suggestion: Serve with nyama choma or pilau.

description: A sweet and tangy Kenyan salsa of ripe mango, tomato, red onion and lime.

steps.instruction: Dice mango and tomato. Finely chop red onion and coriander.
Combine in a bowl and squeeze lime juice over.
Add salt, toss gently and serve fresh.

serving_suggestion: Serve with grilled fish or chicken.

description: A thick, refreshing Kenyan smoothie made with ripe mango, yogurt and banana.

steps.instruction: Peel and chop the mango. Peel the banana if using.
Blend mango, yogurt, banana and sugar until smooth.
Pour into glasses and serve chilled.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a breakfast or snack.

description: A fresh Kenyan salad combining sweet mango and creamy avocado with red onion and lime.

steps.instruction: Dice the mango and avocado. Finely chop the red onion.
Combine in a bowl and squeeze lime juice over.
Add salt, toss gently and serve fresh.

serving_suggestion: Serve with grilled meat or as a side.

description: A sweet and spicy Kenyan mango chutney made with ginger, chilli and lemon.

steps.instruction: Peel and chop the mango. Grate the ginger and finely chop the chilli.
Combine mango, sugar, ginger, chilli and lemon juice in a pot.
Simmer on low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring, until thick and jammy. Cool and store.

serving_suggestion: Serve with grilled meats or rice.

description: A subtly sweet Kenyan rice dish cooked with ripe mango and a touch of sugar.

steps.instruction: Rinse rice. Dice the mango into small cubes.
Bring water to a boil, add rice and salt. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in mango and sugar, cover and cook for 5 more minutes. Fluff and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with grilled fish or as a side.

description: Ripe papaya cubes dressed with lime and a hint of chilli, a refreshing Kenyan fruit salad.

steps.instruction: Peel papaya, remove seeds and cut into cubes.
Squeeze lime juice over the papaya.
Add chilli and mint if using, toss gently and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a light dessert or snack.

description: A smooth, tropical Kenyan smoothie made with ripe papaya, yogurt and banana.

steps.instruction: Peel, deseed and chop the papaya.
Blend papaya, yogurt, banana and sugar until smooth.
Serve chilled.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a breakfast drink.

description: A fresh Kenyan salad of sweet papaya and creamy avocado with lime and red onion.

steps.instruction: Dice papaya and avocado. Finely chop red onion.
Combine and squeeze lime juice over.
Add salt, toss gently and serve fresh.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a side or light meal.

description: A warm Kenyan porridge made with millet flour and sweet ripe papaya, perfect for breakfast.

steps.instruction: Mix millet flour with a little water to form a paste.
Bring remaining water to a boil, stir in the paste and cook for 8–10 minutes until thick.
Mash the papaya and stir into the porridge with milk and sugar. Serve warm.

serving_suggestion: Serve warm for breakfast.

description: Chilled papaya cubes topped with creamy yogurt and a sprinkle of mint, a simple Kenyan dessert.

steps.instruction: Peel, deseed and cube the papaya.
Divide papaya between bowls and spoon yogurt over.
Sprinkle with sugar and mint if using. Serve chilled.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a light dessert.

description: Fresh, tangy Kenyan passion fruit juice sweetened lightly and served chilled.

steps.instruction: Cut passion fruits and scoop pulp into a blender.
Add water and sugar. Blend briefly.
Strain through a sieve to remove seeds. Chill and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve chilled as a refreshing drink.

description: A creamy Kenyan smoothie made with tangy passion fruit, yogurt and banana.

steps.instruction: Scoop passion fruit pulp into a blender.
Add yogurt, banana and sugar. Blend until smooth.
Strain if desired and serve chilled.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a breakfast drink.

description: A Kenyan tomato-onion kachumbari dressed with tangy passion fruit pulp.

steps.instruction: Dice tomatoes and red onion. Chop coriander.
Scoop passion fruit pulp and mix with the vegetables.
Add salt, toss gently and serve fresh.

serving_suggestion: Serve with grilled meat or rice.

description: A tangy Kenyan jam made from passion fruit pulp, sugar and lemon.

steps.instruction: Scoop passion fruit pulp into a pot.
Add sugar and lemon juice. Stir over low heat until sugar dissolves.
Simmer for 20–25 minutes until thick. Cool and store in a jar.

serving_suggestion: Serve with bread, chapati or yogurt.

name_sw: Parfait ya Passion na Maziwa ya Mgando
description: Layers of creamy yogurt, banana and tangy passion fruit, a healthy Kenyan breakfast or dessert.

steps.instruction: Slice the banana. Scoop passion fruit pulp.
Layer yogurt, banana and passion fruit in glasses.
Sprinkle with sugar if using and serve chilled.

serving_suggestion: Serve as breakfast or dessert.

description: Firm green bananas simmered with beef in a rich tomato and onion stew.

steps.instruction: Peel green bananas and cut into chunks. Soak in water.
Brown beef in oil, add onions and garlic and cook until soft. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add green bananas, salt and water. Cover and simmer for 25–30 minutes until bananas and beef are tender.
Serve hot with rice or as a main.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or chapati.

description: Green bananas simmered in a spiced coconut curry with tomatoes and onions.

steps.instruction: Peel green bananas and cut into chunks.
Heat oil and sauté onion until soft. Add curry powder and tomatoes, cook until saucy.
Add green bananas and coconut milk. Simmer for 20–25 minutes until bananas are tender. Season and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or chapati.

description: A hearty Kenyan one-pot dish of green bananas and beans simmered with onions and tomatoes.

steps.instruction: Peel green bananas and cut into chunks.
Sauté onions until golden, add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add green bananas, beans, salt and water. Simmer for 20–25 minutes until bananas are tender. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or as a main.

description: Crispy green banana fries, a Kenyan snack similar to potato chips but with a firmer texture.

steps.instruction: Peel green bananas and cut into thin strips or rounds.
Heat oil in a deep pan. Fry the banana pieces in batches until golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with salt and serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a snack with kachumbari.

description: A comforting Kenyan soup made with green bananas, onions, tomatoes and garlic.

steps.instruction: Peel and chop green bananas. Sauté onions and garlic in oil until soft.
Add tomatoes and cook until softened. Add green bananas and water.
Simmer for 20 minutes until bananas are tender. Season with salt and serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a starter or light meal.

description: A hearty Kenyan stew of green plantains simmered with beef, tomatoes and onions.

steps.instruction: Peel green plantains and cut into chunks. Soak in water.
Brown beef in oil, add onions and garlic and cook until soft. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add plantains, salt and water. Cover and simmer for 25–30 minutes until tender.
Serve hot with rice or as a main.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or chapati.

description: Crispy fried green plantain chips, a popular Kenyan snack.

steps.instruction: Peel green plantains and slice thinly.
Heat oil and fry slices in batches until golden and crisp.
Drain, sprinkle with salt and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a snack.

description: Green plantains and beans simmered together in a tomato-onion sauce, a filling Kenyan meal.

steps.instruction: Peel green plantains and cut into chunks.
Sauté onions until golden, add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add plantains, beans, salt and water. Simmer for 20–25 minutes until plantains are tender. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or as a main.

description: Green plantains simmered in a spiced coconut curry, a coastal Kenyan favourite.

steps.instruction: Peel green plantains and cut into chunks.
Sauté onion until soft, add curry powder and tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add plantains and coconut milk. Simmer for 20–25 minutes until tender. Season and serve.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or chapati.

description: A smooth, filling Kenyan porridge made with green plantains, millet flour and milk.

steps.instruction: Peel and grate green plantains. Mix millet flour with a little water.
Bring remaining water to a boil, add plantains and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in millet paste and cook for 8–10 minutes until thick. Add milk and sugar. Serve warm.

serving_suggestion: Serve warm for breakfast.

description: Sweet ripe plantains cooked with tender beef in a rich tomato sauce.

steps.instruction: Peel ripe plantains and slice thickly. Brown beef in oil.
Add onion and garlic and cook until soft. Add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add plantains, salt and water. Simmer for 20–25 minutes until plantains are soft and beef is tender.
Serve hot with rice or ugali.

serving_suggestion: Serve with rice or chapati.

description: Sweet ripe plantains fried until caramelised, a simple Kenyan snack or side.

steps.instruction: Peel ripe plantains and slice diagonally.
Heat oil and fry slices for 2–3 minutes per side until golden.
Drain, sprinkle with salt and serve warm.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a snack or side.

description: Sweet ripe plantains simmered with beans in a tomato-onion sauce, a comforting Kenyan meal.

steps.instruction: Peel and slice ripe plantains.
Sauté onions until golden, add tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Add plantains and beans, season with salt and simmer for 15–20 minutes until plantains are soft. Serve hot.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a main or side.

description: Sweet ripe plantains simmered in coconut milk with sugar and cardamom, a simple Kenyan dessert.

steps.instruction: Peel and slice ripe plantains.
Combine coconut milk, sugar and cardamom in a pot and bring to a simmer.
Add plantains and cook for 15 minutes until soft and syrupy. Serve warm.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a dessert.

description: A creamy Kenyan smoothie made with sweet ripe plantain, milk and banana.

steps.instruction: Peel and chop the ripe plantain.
Blend plantain, milk, banana and sugar until smooth.
Serve chilled.

serving_suggestion: Serve as a breakfast drink.
